text: A subnet mask is written as 255.255.208.0. What is wrong with it?
choices: Nothing — it is a valid mask
208 is not a contiguous run of ones followed by zeros, so the mask is invalid
Masks may not contain values above 192 in the third octet
It is valid but only for Class B networks
explanation: 208 is 11010000 — ones, then a zero, then a one. A valid mask must be all ones followed by all zeros, which permits only nine octet values (0, 128, 192, 224, 240, 248, 252, 254, 255). RFC 4632 requires contiguity; 208 is most likely a typo for 192 or 224.
